                  "content": "  \"plan\": \"# Implementation Plan: Periodic Location Updates\\n\\n## Overview\\n\\nCurrently, &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; only sends location updates to the server when the location changes significantly (based on distance/accuracy thresholds). This plan adds a time-based criteria: updates will also be sent periodically at a user-configurable interval (1-24 hours), even if the location hasn't changed. This ensures battery level and other metadata stay current on the server.\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\nThe implementation will modify the location update decision logic in &amp;#96;LocationManager.swift&amp;#96; to check both:\\n1. **Location change criteria** (existing): Distance/accuracy thresholds\\n2. **Time-based criteria** (new): Time elapsed since last server update\\n\\n## Implementation Details\\n\\n### 1. Add Setting for Periodic Update Interval\\n\\n**File**: &amp;#96;miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/SettingsManager.swift&amp;#96;\\n\\n- Add new &amp;#96;@Published&amp;#96; property &amp;#96;periodicLocationUpdateIntervalHo [... omitted end of long line]"

              "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 24974,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Control tracking, data retention, server URL, device autolock, accuracy indicators, map type, zoom level, update interval, group zoom‑to‑fit, off‑screen arrows, auto‑refresh, reverse geocoding threshold, navigation mode, and route progress.\\n- View location tracking details or replay the onboarding wizard.\\n- Settings are grouped into tracking, app behavior, map configuration, and navigation sections for easier discovery.\\n\\n- All app preferences are also available in the system Settings app.\\n- New options include: navigation route auto‑update, route progress visualization toggle, a global pulsing/shimmer switch for map markers, and off‑screen arrow visibility.\\n- Bicycle transport mode was removed; existing values fall back to walking for directions and car icons where applicable.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;SettingsManager&amp;#96; stores all preferences in &amp;#96;UserDefaults&amp;#96; and triggers side effects such as permission checks and auto‑refresh.\\n- &amp;#96;iPho [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                  "lineNumber": 25054,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- The status view lists speed and battery (when available) and tracks route‑request statistics over the last 24 hours.\","
                }
              ]

Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

## Cause of the stuck statistics

1. **Widget requests stuck at 1000**  
   The widget and app were storing timestamps as `[Date]` with the default JSON encoding. Only when **recording** a new request did the app prune and trim the list. When you only opened the screen (without a new widget request), it **never pruned** old entries in storage. So you could have 1000 old timestamps; the 24h count was computed correctly from them, but if there was any encoding/decoding or timezone issue, the displayed count could look stuck. Also, the count was only refreshed when the view was on screen (on appear + every 60s).

2. **UpdateLocation (and other API stats) stuck at 2000**  
   Same idea: timestamps were stored with the default `Date` encoding. With 2000 stored entries and possible encoding ambiguity, the “last 24 hours” count could appear stuck at the storage cap.

3. **No refresh when app became active again**  
   Stats were refreshed on appear and every 60s, but not when the app came back from background, so you could look at the screen after hours and still see old numbers until the next timer tick.

## Changes made

### 1. **WidgetRequestCounter** (`miataru/SettingsManagers/WidgetRequestCounter.swift`)

- **Storage format:** Timestamps are now stored as **seconds since 1970** (`[Double]`) instead of `[Date]`, so decoding is unambiguous and the 24h window is reliable.
- **Prune on read:** When you open Location Tracking Details, it **prunes** old timestamps (keep last 7 days, cap at 1000) and **saves** the trimmed list. So storage shrinks over time and the “last 24 hours” count can go down instead of staying at 1000.
- **Backward compatible:** Still loads the old `[Date]` format if present, then saves in the new format when it next writes.

### 2. **Widget extension** (`miataruWidgets/SharedWidgetData.swift`)

- **Same format:** Widget request timestamps are now written as **seconds since 1970** so they match what the app expects and the app’s 24h filter works correctly.
- **Compatibility:** Can still read legacy `[Date]` data, then writes in the new format.

### 3. **APIRequestCounter** (`miataru/SettingsManagers/APIRequestCounter.swift`)

- **Storage format:** Timestamps are now stored as **seconds since 1970** (`[String: [Double]]`) so “last 24 hours” is computed consistently and no longer gets stuck at 2000.
- **Backward compatible:** Still loads legacy `[String: [Date]]` and converts to the new format on save.

### 4. **LocationStatusView** (`miataru/views/iPhone/Settings Views/iPhone_LocationStatusView.swift`)

- **Single refresh path:** All stats (route “today”, widget “last 24h”, and all API “last 24h” counts) are updated in one helper, `refreshAllStatistics()`.
- **Refresh when app becomes active:** Added `onChange(of: scenePhase)` so when the app returns to foreground (e.g. after hours in background), route, widget, and API statistics are refreshed immediately.
- **Same triggers:** Still refreshes on appear and every 60 seconds via the existing timer.

## What you should see now

- **Widget requests (last 24 hours)** and **Updated location calls (last 24 hours)** (and the other API “last 24 hours” stats) will **decrease** as time passes, because:
  - Counts are based on a clear 24h window (seconds since 1970).
  - Old data is pruned and saved when you open the details screen and when the app becomes active.
- **Route requests** (today) was already resetting at midnight; it’s unchanged and still refreshed with the others.
- Opening the app or the Location Tracking Details screen after a long time will show up‑to‑date numbers right away.

If you had already hit the old caps (1000 / 2000), the first time you open the screen after this update it will prune and re-save. After that, the 24h counts will roll off correctly as time passes.

Summary of what was committed:

**Commit:** `3b97f69a` — **Fix location tracking details statistics not resetting (24h counts stuck)**

**Problem:** In Location Tracking Details, “Widget requests (last 24 hours)” and “Updated location calls (last 24 hours)” (and other API 24h stats) stayed at 1000 and 2000 and did not decrease over time.

**Cause:**  
1. Timestamps were stored with the default JSON `Date` encoding, so decoding was ambiguous and 24h filtering did not roll off correctly.  
2. `WidgetRequestCounter` only pruned when recording new requests, not when the details screen was opened, so storage stayed at the cap and the displayed count could not drop.

**Fix:**  
- **WidgetRequestCounter:** Store timestamps as seconds since 1970 (`[Double]`), prune and save when `updateCount()` runs so storage shrinks and the 24h count can decrease; still load legacy `[Date]`.  
- **SharedWidgetData (widget):** Write widget request timestamps as seconds since 1970 to match the app; still load legacy `[Date]`.  
- **APIRequestCounter:** Store timestamps as seconds since 1970 (`[String: [Double]]`); still load legacy `[String: [Date]]`.  
- **LocationStatusView:** Refresh all stats (route, widget, API) in `refreshAllStatistics()`, and call it on appear, when the app becomes active (`scenePhase`), and every 60s.
